business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as engineering high-performance combustion equipment and technology-based solutions, with 15+ years of experience, a global technology partnership and integrated engineering plus manufacturing; end-use industries listed are refining, petrochemicals, fertilisers, hydrogen and steel.
- Strategic collaboration with JNK Global (Korea) is said to give access to global expertise, design know-how and proven references, with JNK India carrying design, engineering, manufacturing and EPC.
- Claims high entry barriers via a customer qualification funnel (pre-qualification, technical evaluation, commercial evaluation, vendor approval, execution, repeat orders), where 'only a few vendors enter the approved vendor list' and consistent performance builds preferred-vendor status.
- The deck itself cites the cancelled June 8, 2026 export order as evidence of the barriers: it was cancelled solely because the requisite technical approval from the licensor could not be secured, 'highlighting the high entry barriers in the industry related to technical approvals and a proven track record.'
- Core solutions are framed as core equipment in process plants, custom-engineered per project, high engineering intensity, critical for plant efficiency and reliability, with long operating life; waste-gas systems are framed as mandatory, mission-critical safety equipment.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order cancellation] The large export order received on June 8, 2026 was cancelled solely due to inability to secure the requisite technical approval from the licensor; the deck states this was an isolated incident, with no material costs incurred and no execution having commenced.
- [JV structure] The Chemdist joint venture is held JNK India 51% / Chemdist Technology 49%, with Chemdist contributing proprietary technologies and IP, advanced R&D and process innovation, and JNK contributing EPC execution, manufacturing and global project execution.
- [New consolidation] The deck repeatedly footnotes that Q1FY27 Total Income includes Revenue of Rs 16.5 cr from JNK Chemdist Limited, which was not part of Q1FY26 — i.e. the YoY comparison is not like-for-like.
- [Restatement] The deck states financial information for previous periods has been regrouped/reclassified to conform to appropriate presentation and comparability, wherever necessary.
- [Board] Board includes Arvind Kamath (Chairperson & WTD), Goutam Rampelli (Vice Chairperson & WTD), Dipak Bharuka (CEO & WTD) and Bang Hee Kim (Non-Executive Director, formerly DL E&C CO and adjunct professor at Yonsei University), reflecting the Korean partnership at board level.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin 14.3% (vs guided 13-14%); Pressure from Rs 9.26 Mn labor code charge; Accounting shift from output to input method normalized margins after legacy project drag; Material cost 74% (down from 78%), expected range 70-75% depending on service mix.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total ~Rs 1,700 Cr (Jan 1); Includes Rs 1,050 Cr booked from BPCL Bina (of larger contract), with Rs 400-600 Cr pending over next 2 quarters; Chemdist JV order book ~Rs 100 Cr; Execution timeline avg 2-2.5 years.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: JNK India delivered a blowout Q3 with revenue doubling YoY and EBITDA tripling, driven by strong execution in refining verticals and a shift to input-based accounting, while securing a robust pipeline including a potential $140M+ Dangote repeat opportunity and early traction from its Green Hydrogen JV.

open.item: First US order (CVR Energy refinery expansion via KBR) is a supply-only fired heater with a delivery period of about 15 months.
Two near-term opportunities (one Middle East waste gas handling ~INR 200-250 crores, one India clean fuel ~INR 200-250 crores) expected to finalize in the next two to three months / a quarter.
Chemdist subsidiary margins (low in its first quarter due to startup expenses) expected to improve from Q4 onwards to at least similar margins as JNK India.
BPCL Bina order (INR 1,050 crores booked from JNK Global) has no revenue booked to date; only ~3%-4% to be booked in Q4 FY26, with the majority (~50%-60%) booked in FY27.
Maintaining the EBITDA margin guidance of 13% to 14% given last year; Q3 EBITDA was 14.3% (would have been 15%+ before the ~INR 9.26 million new labour code impact).
Reaffirmed the ~40% growth guidance for FY26, expecting to be within the guided range.
Targeting 15%-25% market share of the ~INR 4,000 crores opportunity in FY25 and FY26.
HPCL order to largely complete by March 2026; Reliance order to spill to Q1 of next year (FY27).
A further BPCL Bina order (from the existing JNK Global contract) worth anywhere between INR 400 to INR 600 crores is yet to be received, expected in the next two quarters or so.

Dangote refinery doubling in Nigeria is a large upcoming opportunity for fired heaters (prior contract was ~$140 million ~10 years ago, prices roughly doubled) plus four fertilizer reformer packages ($30-40 million each); order finalization expected around Q3 FY27.
Broadly agreed that with an opening order book near INR 2,000 crores next year, JNK could execute roughly INR 1,000-odd crores of revenue in FY27 (formal guidance deferred until Q4 completes).
A healthy book-to-bill ratio for JNK is around 2 to 2.5, given an average execution time frame of 2-2.5 years.
Material cost should stay in the range of about 70% to 75% of revenue (was 74% in Q3, down from 78%), potentially lower when the services component is higher.

Chemdist subsidiary contributed about INR 23 crores revenue in Q3 FY26 (its first quarter) with an order book of ~INR 100 crores as of 1 Jan; expected to contribute ~10% (10%-15%) of JNK India standalone revenue in the first couple of years.

Continued R&D on green hydrogen, carbon capture and sustainable fuels via the Chemdist JV (a few patents already, one Hydrogen Valley pilot project to take off soon); larger commercialized opportunities expected in about two years.
Despite the stock price fall, no specific buyback plans as of now.
Historical order hit rate is about 25% of finalizations; expects a better balance hit rate after losing one large finalization in Q1 FY26.
Suntech Infra arbitration petition on the Dahej (Reliance) contract does not affect execution timeline and will not have significant financial implications.

verdicts.item: Management expects around 25% to 30% year-on-year revenue increase and to exceed that in the next couple of years.
verdicts.note: Q3FY26 revenue Rs2,062.3mn 'Y-o-Y growth of 112.8%'; 9M revenue ~Rs4,934mn - far exceeds the 25-30% medium-term target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Bid pipeline is about INR 4,000 crores for exports plus about INR 4,000 crores for domestic (separate), expected to finalize in about 6 to 8 months after bidding.
verdicts.note: two opportunities '~Rs. 200 to 250 crores each... next two to three months'; Dangote large but FY27 - pipeline present, the ~INR8,000cr figure not restated.

verdicts.item: Aspiration for green/renewable energy line to become at least about 30% of total revenue in 3 to 5 years.
verdicts.note: 'we expect revenue of about 10% or so for the first couple of years from the subsidiaries'; order book ~Rs100cr - progress toward the ~30% renewable aspiration. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Whatever the FY25 revenue shortfall, JNK must catch up and deliver far better growth in FY26 (aiming to maintain the original FY26 projection) due to committed customer delivery timelines.
verdicts.note: Q3 revenue +112.8% YoY, 9M ~Rs4,934mn vs FY25 9M ~Rs2,950mn; 'delivering what we have promised at the beginning of the year' - strong FY26 catch-up delivered.

verdicts.item: Two large US EPC-company projects (included in the export pipeline) expected to finalize in the next 3 to 6 months.
verdicts.note: 'in U.S. ... more opportunities could come up, but not so large size opportunities are coming up as of now' - the two large US EPC-company projects did not finalize in the expected 3-6 months.

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed full-year FY26 revenue growth guidance of 40% to 50%.
verdicts.note: 'we gave a range so we will definitely be within the range'; Q3 +112.8%, 9M revenue ~Rs4,934mn - tracking within/above the 40-50% range. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed FY26 EBITDA margin guidance of roughly 12% to 13%.
verdicts.note: Q3 EBITDA margin 14.3% (15%+ ex-labour code); 9M ~12% - margins at/above the 12-13% FY26 guidance. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Margin compression (Q1 EBITDA 7%) from legacy/former projects is a temporary pain expected to continue into Q2 FY26; legacy order book likely to get over by Q2 FY26.
verdicts.note: 'the old legacy projects... now they are almost closed, so that's why we see normal margins now' - margin compression resolved, legacy cleared.

verdicts.item: From Q3 and Q4 FY26 majority of revenue comes from new (input-method) projects, so there will be no volatility on profit margins and a jump to the guided range is needed.
verdicts.note: 'now they are almost closed, so that's why we see normal margins now. And this would continue' - Q3 revenue majority from new projects, margins jumped to guided range.

verdicts.item: Sustainable EBITDA margin of 13% to 15% expected once the legacy projects are over.
verdicts.note: original Q3 margin '15% plus in terms of EBITDA', 14.3% after labour code; 'normal margins now... would continue' - within/above the 13-15% sustainable range. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Current order book (~INR 983 crores / INR 9,828 million as of June 2025) would get executed up to Q1 of FY27.
verdicts.note: legacy closed; HPCL completing by March, Reliance Q1FY27 - the ~INR983cr book largely executing by Q1FY27 as stated, with tail; overall book grown.

verdicts.item: Reliance and HPCL projects on track to deliver revenues in Q3/Q4 FY26 and be completed by worst-case Q1 of next financial year (FY27).
verdicts.note: 'HPCL would largely get completed by March. And Reliance would spill to Q1 of next year' - on track exactly as committed, not yet complete.

wtt.summary: 43% guidance hit (21 chains); 2/6 projects on-time; 1 expired; 27% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and celebratory after a strong Q3 that delivered on the year's promises; management candidly attributed margin normalization to the accounting-method change (not pricing power) and flagged the new labour code impact, while deferring FY27 guidance until Q4 completes.

one-line thesis: JNK India delivered a blowout Q3 with revenue doubling YoY and EBITDA tripling, driven by strong execution in refining verticals and a shift to input-based accounting, while securing a robust pipeline including a potential $140M+ Dangote repeat opportunity and early traction from its Green Hydrogen JV.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs 2,062 Mn (+112.8% YoY); EBITDA: Rs 295 Mn (+202.8% YoY, 14.3% margin); PAT: Rs 180 Mn (+534.1% YoY, 8.7% margin); Order Book: ~Rs 1,700 Cr (as of Jan 1); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but working capital limits utilized (Rs 470 Cr non-fund, Rs 70 Cr fund); One-offs: Rs 9.26 Mn charge for new labor code impact recognized in Q3.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~40% for FY26 (maintained); Margin: 13-14% EBITDA (maintained despite labor code hit); Order Inflow: Expect Rs 400-600 Cr from BPCL Bina in next 2 quarters; Rs 200-250 Cr each from Middle East waste gas and domestic clean fuel projects in ~1 quarter; Capex/Commissioning: JV pilot projects taking off soon.
order book & pipeline: Total ~Rs 1,700 Cr (Jan 1); Includes Rs 1,050 Cr booked from BPCL Bina (of larger contract), with Rs 400-600 Cr pending over next 2 quarters; Chemdist JV order book ~Rs 100 Cr; Execution timeline avg 2-2.5 years.
segment / subsidiary detail: Fired Heaters: Core driver, major exposure to Dangote (Nigeria) and BPCL Bina; Flares/Incinerators: Driven by regulatory retrofit/compliance rather than greenfield; Green Hydrogen/Chemdist: Early stage, Rs 23 Cr revenue in Q3, targeting 10-15% of standalone revenue in 2-3 years; Biogas/CBG: Technology stabilization challenges, policy support via budget excise exemption.
growth verticals / optionality: Dangote Refinery expansion (doubling capacity) offers ~$140M fired heater opportunity + 4 reformer packages ($30-40M each); Qualification for large cracking furnace contracts opens door to bigger petchem projects; JV with Chemdist provides IP-led growth in green hydrogen/CCUS; Middle East export pipeline (Rs 200-250 Cr imminent).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 14.3% (vs guided 13-14%); Pressure from Rs 9.26 Mn labor code charge; Accounting shift from output to input method normalized margins after legacy project drag; Material cost 74% (down from 78%), expected range 70-75% depending on service mix.
capex / expansion: No major standalone capex mentioned; Fabrication capacity (Mundra) currently underutilized due to lack of export execution, not a bottleneck as model relies on customer-approved shops near sites; Focus on R&D and pilot projects for Green Hydrogen/CBG via JV.
capital allocation: Working capital limits sufficient (Rs 500 Cr non-fund, Rs 100 Cr fund); Bank guarantee burden eased via JNK Global partnership for large contracts (e.g., BPCL); Performance guarantees (10% of contract value) will remain blocked post-project completion.
risks & watch-items: Execution timing slippage (Reliance spilling to Q1 FY27); Dangote order finalization uncertainty (expected Q3 FY27); CBG technology/feedstock stabilization issues limiting domestic uptake; Dependency on large lump-sum orders causing quarterly volatility; Labor code compliance costs.
management quality / tone: Confident and optimistic; Emphasizes strong order book, strategic positioning in energy transition, and successful JV ramp-up; Acknowledges near-term margin pressure from one-offs but reaffirms guidance; Cautious on CBG timeline due to tech hurdles.
non-obvious takeaways: Accounting policy shift (output to input method) is the primary driver of margin normalization, not operating leverage or pricing; Mundra facility utilization is low not due to demand but lack of specific export projects under execution; JV revenue (Rs 23 Cr) already flowing in first quarter of operation, faster than typical R&D spin-offs; Bank guarantee structure via JNK Global significantly de-risks balance sheet for large tenders.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for high-efficiency fired heaters and reformers in refinery expansion | JNK India Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of Dangote Refinery expansion ($140M+ opportunity) and BPCL Bina execution; unique qualification for large cracking furnaces. |
| Technology stabilization and feedstock issues in CBG sector | Pure-play CBG developers | loser | Med | Sector facing delays due to tech/feedstock hurdles, though JNK is positioned to benefit once solutions stabilize via European partnerships. |
| Scaling green hydrogen production under National Mission | Chemdist Group (Unlisted JV Partner) | beneficiary | High | JV with JNK provides commercial pathway for Chemdist's IP in green hydrogen/CCUS, leveraging JNK's execution muscle. |
